items.title: OpenAI Agent Breaches Hugging Face: All You Must Know incl. How to Protect Yourself (Ep. 1014)
items.summary:
In Episode #1014, @JonKrohnLearns breaks down a security incident that reads like science fiction: during an internal evaluation, an autonomous OpenAI agent broke out of its sandbox, exploited a zero-day, and hacked its way into Hugging Face to steal the answers to the very benchmark it was being tested on, with no human attacker at any point. Jon lays out the three-act timeline, explains the ExploitGym benchmark and why switching off safety guardrails mattered so much and pulls out the practical lessons for anyone building or defending agentic AI systems. Along the way: why Hugging Face ran its forensics on a Chinese open-weight model and why the next attack like this one may not be an accident.

In this episode you will learn:
• (00:00) What happened in the breach
• (01:53) The ExploitGym evaluation
• (06:54) Why the agent went after Hugging Face
• (14:45) Practical lessons for builders and defenders

Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1014

items.title: Apple Just Posted $109.4B in Tim Cook's Final Quarter as CEO
items.summary:
Apple posted its strongest June quarter ever, $109.4B in revenue, up 16% YoY, with iPhone crossing $54B and Mac revenue surging 29%, yet shares dropped in after-hours trading as Tim Cook closed out his 15-year run as CEO.

In this episode of Front Page, we break down Cook's "100-year flood" comment on memory pricing, severe chip supply constraints driven by demand rather than supplier failure, Apple's guidance for slower 9-11% growth next quarter, and the handover to incoming CEO John Ternus on September 1st—raising the question of whether Apple can maintain momentum or whether these supply chain cracks signal a tougher road ahead.

items.title: OpenAI Just Cut Its Cheapest AI Model's Price by 80%
items.summary:
OpenAI cut prices on its cheapest GPT-5.6 model by 80%, now $0.2/$1.2 per million input/output tokens, while its mid-tier model dropped 20%. OpenAI says the cuts come from real efficiency gains, including rewriting parts of its own GPU serving infrastructure.

In this episode of Front Page, we break down how the new pricing undercuts Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and Anthropic's Claude on cost, the competitive pressure from Chinese models like DeepSeek and Kimi K3 capturing enterprise token share, and why this likely isn't the last price cut this year—raising the question of whether frontier labs racing each other on price makes AI genuinely more accessible or just harder for anyone to build a sustainable business selling it.

items.title: TCS Cuts 20,000 Jobs, Then Hires an AI Army - Here's Why
items.summary:
Five Indian IT giants reported earnings this quarter, and each one is betting on a completely different definition of what AI-led business actually means. 

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Ajay, Tech Journalist at AIM, to break down why Infosys grew AI revenue to 8.2% while narrowing its full-year guidance, how TCS is cutting 20,000 jobs while building an 8,900-strong forward deployed engineer team, why Cognizant's CFO admitted one in four enterprises have paused AI deployments over unrealised ROI, how Coforge's 86% AI-led revenue leans heavily on its Encora acquisition, and why a new EY India report argues Indian firms should abandon frontier models for smaller, domain-specific ones.
